summary: Caribbean residence-by-investment schemes in Bermuda, the Bahamas, the Cayman Islands, the Turks and Caicos Islands and Anguilla are well documented in law (acts, regulations, fee schedules), with terms traced over time; Barbados and the Dominican Republic only thinly. Official numbers exist only for Bermuda (ministerial press tables of approved applications, holders and investment by type, 2021-2025); the Bahamas, Cayman, TCI and Anguilla publish no counts of investor residence grants or revenue that could be found.

sources.title: Immigration (Amendment) Bill, 2021
sources.publisher: Government of The Bahamas (published by the Ministry of Economic Affairs)
sources.covers: Inserts s.17A (economic permanent residence certificate) into the Immigration Act Ch.191; 90-day annual residence; 10-year hold; deemed approval after 3 months; in force 1 July 2021.
sources.notes: Bill text as tabled with the 2021/22 budget. The enacted Act was not retrieved, but s.17A is cited as in force by the 2024 amendment bill and by the Department of Immigration fee scale.

sources.title: Immigration (Amendment) Bill, 2024
sources.publisher: Office of the Attorney General, The Bahamas
sources.covers: Amends s.17A: $1m investment for 10 years in real estate or Central Bank zero coupon bonds; reinstatement fee; deed of gift excluded; in force 1 January 2025.
sources.notes: Bill text (file name suggests posting on 28 Apr 2025). The gazetted Act was not found; the Budget Communication confirms the 1 January 2025 start.

sources.title: Budget Communication 2024/2025
sources.publisher: Government of The Bahamas (Prime Minister and Minister of Finance Philip Davis)
sources.covers: Announces economic permanent residency minimum rising from $750,000 (real estate only) to $1.0 million in real estate and/or Central Bank zero coupon bonds from 1 January 2025; $500 reinstatement fee.
sources.notes: Budget speech; amounts in Bahamian dollars (printed "$"), at par with the US dollar.

sources.title: Immigration Fee Scale
sources.publisher: Bahamas Department of Immigration
sources.covers: Current fees for Economic Permanent Residence Certificates under s.17A ($25,000 with right to work in own business; $20,000 without).

From 31 March 2023 the same BD$2,500,000 applies under the EIRC policy (bmu-mel-eirc-policy-2023, p. 1: "not less than BD$2,500,000"), with the residential certificate granted at once instead of after five years.

program_terms.quote: As a result, Bermuda Government bonds are removed from the list of qualifying investment options with immediate effect.
program_terms.notes: Bond route (5-year hold) existed from launch; removed by announcement of 9 June 2024. Minimum was the general $2.5M threshold. Only one application (two holders, $2.6m) used it.

program_terms.location: para "The effective date of the policy..."
program_terms.quote: A fee of $2,625 will be charged for the issuance of the certificate, in accordance with the existing Government Fees Schedule.

program_terms.quote: those applying for permanent residency will now have to spend at least US$1.5 million on a Bahamian home to get fast-tracked by the Immigration Department.
program_terms.notes: Administrative policy (2011 National Investment Policy), not law: buying a home of this value earned "accelerated" (fast-tracked) consideration; previously US$500,000. Lower-value owners could still apply on the ordinary route. valid_from is the day the policy was tabled (18 April 2011, per later reports); end date unknown. The MOFA page (bhs-mofa-pr-page-2026) still mentions BS$1.5 million "speedy consideration".

program_terms.quote: Before, the requirement only called for $750,000 in Real Estate investments.
program_terms.notes: Start date not documented officially: a former attorney general said the threshold was raised from $500,000 "as recently as 2018" (bhs-tribune-delaney-2021), and the Minister in June 2021 described "the present, narrow route of acquiring Bahamian real estate valued at $750,000 or more" (bhs-tribune-epr-floor-2021). From 1 July 2021 the amount was set by ministerial order under s.17A; the order itself was not found.

program_terms.quote: has made an investment of one million dollars for a minimum period of ten years- (i) in real estate in The Bahamas; or (ii) in Zero Coupon Bonds issued by the Central Bank of The Bahamas
program_terms.notes: Asset must be held 10 years. Deeds of gift excluded. Bill text; start date per s.1(2) and the 2024 Budget Communication.

program_terms.quote: has made an investment of one million dollars for a minimum period of ten years- (i) in real estate in The Bahamas; or (ii) in Zero Coupon Bonds issued by the Central Bank of The Bahamas
program_terms.notes: Central Bank of The Bahamas zero coupon bonds; proceeds earmarked for education, health, Family Island infrastructure or youth and sports (new s.17A(9)). program_terms.notes: Current fee read 2026-10-02; start date unknown.

program_terms.quote: We are also imposing a $500 reinstatement fee for Permanent Resident Applications which have been successfully concluded but not finalized after 90 days.
program_terms.notes: Applies to all permanent residence applications; written into s.17A(1A) for economic PR by the 2024 bill. Start date assumed to match the bill (1 Jan 2025); the budget does not give one.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant, Grand Cayman (of which CI$250,000 in developed real estate)

program_terms.notes: Also needed a continuous annual income of CI$120,000. Cayman Brac/Little Cayman: CI$250,000 (CI$125,000 real estate) and CI$75,000 income. Earlier start date not established. valid_to is the gazette date of the 2017 change.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant, Grand Cayman (of which CI$500,000 in developed real estate)

program_terms.notes: Plus annual income of at least CI$120,000 or a CI$400,000 deposit with a local regulated institution. Cayman Brac/Little Cayman: CI$500,000 (CI$250,000 real estate). Made 17 May 2017, gazetted 26 May 2017; commencement date not stated. Certificate valid 25 years, no right to work.

program_terms.quote: Issue of Residency Certificate for Persons of Independent Means 20,000
program_terms.notes: Plus CI$500 application fee and CI$1,000 per dependant (made annual from 2017 by cym-imm-amend4-regs-2017). Same CI$20,000 in the 2018 revision (p. 32). program_terms.quote: that he has invested one million six hundred thousand dollars in developed real estate in the Cayman Islands.
program_terms.notes: Developed real estate only. Quota of 250 certificates a year (reg 14B(2)). Start date: certificate created by the Immigration (Amendment) Law 2012; the regulation setting CI$1.6m was not retrieved.

program_terms.quote: that the applicant has invested two million dollars in developed real estate in the Cayman Islands
program_terms.notes: Still CI$2 million under the Immigration (Transition) Act (the 2025 Act refers to the "prescribed sum"). From 1 May 2026 the certificate is for 10 years, renewable indefinitely (cym-imm-trans-amend-act-2025, s.17).

program_terms.quote: an applicant for a Certificate of Direct Investment shall satisfy the Chief Immigration Officer that he proposes to invest or has invested a sum of at least one million dollars in an employment generating business.

program_terms.quote: Issue of Certificate of Direct Investment 20,000
program_terms.notes: Plus CI$1,000 application fee and dependant fees; holder also pays an annual fee equal to a work permit fee. Draft 2026 fee: CI$50,000 (not confirmed).

events.title: Bermuda launches the Economic Investment Certificate
events.description: The EIC lets foreign nationals who invest at least $2.5 million in Bermuda live there for five years and then seek a Residential Certificate. It replaced Residential Certificate policies of 2003 and 2015 that targeted the "globally retired" with "substantial means" and led to court challenges.
events.quote: The effective date of the policy is  1st March 2021 .

events.title: EIC becomes the Economic Investment Residential Certificate (no five-year wait)
events.description: The Minister may grant a Residential Certificate under s.32(5) of the Bermuda Immigration and Protection Act straight away, instead of after five years on an EIC, citing Bermuda's ageing population.
events.quote: This revised policy will be made effective 31 March 2023 by order of the Minister.

events.title: Government bonds removed as a qualifying investment
events.description: Bermuda dropped Government bonds from EIRC investments because ownership was hard to track for five years and no new bonds were planned; one application (two holders, $2.6m) had used the route.
events.quote: Bermuda Government bonds are removed from the list of qualifying investment options with immediate effect.

events.title: Bahamas raises fast-track permanent residency home value to US$1.5 million
events.description: Prime Minister Ingraham's National Investment Policy raised the home value giving accelerated consideration of permanent residence from US$500,000 to US$1.5 million. Date is when the policy was tabled (later reports); the RTC report is dated 20 April 2011.
events.quote: Previously, a policy designed to attract foreign investors allowed a person owning a home worth US$500,000 or more to receive speedy consideration by immigration officials.

events.title: Economic permanent residence put in statute (s.17A Immigration Act)
events.description: The Immigration (Amendment) Act 2021 created the economic permanent residence certificate: purchase of a residence and/or investments of amounts set by ministerial order, 90 days' residence a year, 10-year hold of the investment, and deemed approval three months after a complete application.
events.quote: This Act shall come into force on the 1st day of July, 2021.

events.title: Budget raises the economic PR minimum to $1 million and adds Central Bank bonds
events.description: The 2024/25 Budget Communication announced a $1.0 million minimum in real estate and/or Central Bank zero coupon bonds, held for 10 years, from 1 January 2025, and a ban on qualifying through deeds of gift.
events.quote: This will now increase to $1.0 million in real estate investments and or the purchase of Zero Coupon Bonds from the Central Bank of The Bahamas.

events.title: New $1 million economic permanent residence rules take effect
events.description: Amended s.17A requires a $1 million investment for at least ten years in Bahamian real estate or Central Bank zero coupon bonds; bond proceeds earmarked for education, health, Family Island infrastructure or youth and sports.
events.quote: This Act shall come into operation on the 1st day of January 2025.

events.title: Practitioners say permanent residents were flipping qualifying property
events.description: Reacting to the 10-year hold, a former MP and lawyer said holders had obtained permanent residency and then sold the qualifying property.
events.quote: People were getting permanent residency, saying thank you very much and selling the place.

events.title: Cayman creates permanent residence for persons of independent means
events.description: The Immigration (Amendment) Law 2012 inserted s.34A (certificate of permanent residence for persons of independent means, by investment in developed real estate, without the right to work) and s.37D (residency certificate for a substantial business presence). Date is the gazette publication; commencement not checked.
events.quote: TO CREATE A NEW CATEGORY OF PERMANENT RESIDENCE FOR PERSONS OF INDEPENDENT MEANS AND A NEW RESIDENCE CATEGORY FOR PERSONS WHO ESTABLISH A SUBSTANTIAL BUSINESS PRESENCE

events.title: Cayman raises independent-means thresholds (CI$2m permanent; CI$1m 25-year)
events.description: Regulations made on 17 May 2017 and gazetted on 26 May raised the permanent residence threshold from CI$1.6m to CI$2m in developed real estate, and the 25-year residency certificate from CI$500,000 to CI$1m (half in real estate), and made the CI$1,000 dependant fee annual.
events.quote: that the applicant has invested two million dollars in developed real estate in the Cayman Islands

events.title: Residency certificates move to WORC under the Immigration (Transition) Law
events.description: The Immigration (Transition) Law 2018 moved independent-means and direct investment certificates to the Director of Workforce Opportunities and Residency Cayman (WORC); the Cabinet sets a gazetted quota for permanent certificates.
events.quote: Government’s plans call for both departments to become officially operational on 1st January, 2019.

events.title: Independent-means permanent residence becomes a 10-year certificate
events.description: The Immigration (Transition) (Amendment and Validation) Act 2025 (in force 1 May 2026) makes the certificate valid for ten years, renewable indefinitely, after which the holder may apply for naturalisation; the qualifying investment must be held at the time of application; holders of direct investment and business presence certificates must file annual declarations. Applications made before 1 May 2026 follow the old law.
events.quote: for a Certificate of Permanent Residence for Persons of Independent Means, which if granted will be for a period of ten years

events.title: Draft fees would double the independent-means permanent residence fee to CI$200,000
events.description: Consultation draft of the Immigration (Transition) (Fees) Regulations 2026 proposed CI$200,000 for the permanent certificate (from CI$100,000), CI$50,000 for the 25-year residency certificate and for the Certificate of Direct Investment (from CI$20,000), and CI$3,000 dependant fees. Adoption not confirmed.
events.quote: Issue fee for Certificate of Permanent Residence for Persons of Independent Means 200,000

events.title: Commission of Inquiry reports complaints of PRC and Belongership grants for bribes
events.description: The Auld Commission of Inquiry into corruption, whose report led the UK to suspend self-government in August 2009, recorded complaints that Belongership and Permanent Residence Certificates were granted in breach of the law in return for bribes, with applications driven by ministers.
events.quote: The complaints are of grant of Belongership or Permanent Resident Certificates in breach of the legal requirements in return for bribes to Ministers or officials

events.title: TCI introduces a 10-year investor residence permit; PRC moratorium lifted 10 September 2012
events.description: New immigration rules signed on 23 July 2012 created a long-term residence permit for investors of US$500,000 (Providenciales/West Caicos) or US$250,000 (other islands) and lifted the moratorium on PRC applications on 10 September 2012, without an investor route to PRC at first.
events.quote: From 13th August, it will be possible for someone who has invested $500,000.00 or more in Providenciales or West Caicos, or $250,000.00 or more in Grand Turk or the family Islands, to obtain a residence permit for up to ten years.

events.title: TCI reintroduces permanent residence by investment
events.description: New regulations restored a PRC investor route (home of US$300,000/1,000,000 or business of US$750,000/1,500,000 depending on island), with a Governor's undertaking in advance, a US$25,000 fee and a cap of 200 PRCs in the first year. Reported by a law firm on 1 October 2013.
events.quote: The Turks and Caicos Islands (TCI) has just enacted a revamped investor residency programme, entitling successful applicants to a permanent residence certificate (PRC).

events.title: TCI investor PRC holders must keep the investment five years and report yearly
events.description: L.N. 34/2018 bars sale of the qualifying home or business for five years unless reinvested within 12 months, requires notice of disposal and an annual report, with a US$1,500 fine for failing to report; it does not apply to PRCs issued before 15 June 2018.
events.quote: Regulations 14 to 16 do not apply to an investment in a home, business or enterprise which was subject of an application of a Permanent Residence Certificate issued prior to 15 June 2018.

events.title: Anguilla Economic Residence Act in force
events.description: The Act (No. 15 of 2019) created residence by investment through approved real estate or the Capital Development Fund, a retroactive route for existing property owners, and residence for tax purposes.
events.quote: Act 15/2019, in force 3 June 2019

events.title: Executive Council asks for the residency scheme to be put in primary legislation
events.description: Before the Act, investment PR was granted case by case under s.24(1) of the Immigration and Passport Act and the Permanent Residence Permit (Amendment) Regulations 2018; Council extended the retroactive fast-track window to 30 June 2019.
events.quote: asked that consideration be given to framing this initiative in primary legislation rather than regulations.

events.title: Anguilla's fund route had never been open
events.description: Executive Council noted that the US$150,000 Capital Development Fund route in the Act had not been available because the fund had not been established, and moved to set it up.
events.quote: However, this option was not available to interested persons because the fund was not established.

events.quote: Permanent Residence Certificate

events.title: Dominican migration office and ProDominicana agree to fast-track investor residence
events.description: A two-year cooperation agreement to validate ProDominicana investment certificates automatically; the migration director said investor residence would take no more than a month and a half and cited a US$250,000 amount.
events.quote: se dará la misma facilidad, pero con un monto menor de 250 mil dólares, atendiendo al tamaño de la economía local.

events.title: Investor residence procedures added to the single investment window

programs.name: Economic Investment Residential Certificate (EIRC; Economic Investment Certificate and Residential Certificate policy until 31 March 2023)
programs.notes: Ministerial policy under s.32(5) of the Bermuda Immigration and Protection Act 1956, not a separate statute. Investment of at least BD$2.5 million (real estate, new or existing business, charity, Sinking Fund, Trust Fund, other approved ventures; Government bonds until 9 June 2024). From 2021 to March 2023 investors first got a five-year Economic Investment Certificate, then could apply for a Residential Certificate; since 31 March 2023 the Residential Certificate (indefinite residence, automatic work approval for the investor's own business) is granted at once, subject to keeping the investment and spending 90 days a year in Bermuda for five years. Replaced the 2003 and 2015 Residential Certificate policies for wealthy retirees. Not a route to Bermudian status or citizenship by itself. Cumulative figures from the Ministry: 79 approved applications, 188 holders and $604.9m associated investment by 5 November 2025.

programs.name: Bahamas Economic Permanent Residence (economic permanent residence certificate, s.17A Immigration Act Ch. 191)
programs.notes: Before July 2021, investors applied for ordinary permanent residence under the Immigration Act with administrative "accelerated consideration" for home buyers (US$500,000, raised to US$1.5m in 2011; a $750,000 real estate threshold applied by 2019-2021). Section 17A (in force 1 July 2021) made it statutory: a home and/or investment of a ministerially prescribed amount, 90 days' residence a year, investment kept 10 years. From 1 January 2025: $1 million in real estate or Central Bank zero coupon bonds for 10 years. Certificates are for life; right to work only in own business. Fees $25,000 (with right to work) or $20,000. Permanent residence does not lead to citizenship automatically. No official count of economic PR grants was found. Listed by the OECD in 2018 as potentially high-risk for CRS avoidance.

programs.name: Cayman Islands Residency Certificate for Persons of Independent Means (25-year)
programs.notes: Section 41 of the Immigration (Transition) Act (s.34 of the former Immigration Law). 25-year certificate, renewable, without the right to work. Since May 2017: CI$1m invested of which CI$500,000 in developed real estate on Grand Cayman (half on the Sister Islands), plus CI$120,000 annual income or a CI$400,000 local deposit; holders must be present 30 days a year. Issue fee CI$20,000 (draft 2026: CI$50,000). Launch date not established (predates the 2014 revision; the Act refers to a separate retirees' certificate under the 2003 Law). No official counts found.

programs.name: Cayman Islands Certificate of Permanent Residence for Persons of Independent Means
programs.notes: Created by the Immigration (Amendment) Law 2012 (s.34A, now s.42 of the Immigration (Transition) Act). Requires investment in developed real estate: CI$1.6m, CI$2m since May 2017. Issue fee CI$100,000 (draft 2026: CI$200,000); quota 250 a year. No right to work unless varied by the Board. From 1 May 2026 the certificate is for 10 years, renewable indefinitely, and the holder may then apply for naturalisation as a British Overseas Territories citizen (residence rules of the British Nationality Act still apply). No official counts found.

programs.name: Cayman Islands Certificate of Direct Investment
programs.notes: Section 47 of the Immigration (Transition) Act (s.37A of the former Law). Investment of at least CI$1m in a licensed employment-generating business in which the holder has substantial management control; 25-year certificate with right to work in that business; audited accounts and job details at years 2 and 5. Issue fee CI$20,000 (draft 2026: CI$50,000). Launch date not established. No counts found.

programs.name: Cayman Islands Residency Certificate (Substantial Business Presence)
programs.notes: Created by the Immigration (Amendment) Law 2012 (s.37D, now s.50). For owners or senior managers of an approved category of business (fund administration, insurance, family office, exempted companies etc.) with physical premises and at least four full-time resident staff; no fixed investment amount. Issue fee CI$5,000 (draft 2026: CI$12,500). No counts found.

programs.name: Turks and Caicos Islands Permanent Residence Certificate by investment (investor routes, Immigration Regulations reg 13(2)(f)-(h),(k))
programs.notes: Under the Immigration Ordinance (Cap. 5.01, Ordinance 19 of 2015) and Immigration Regulations (L.N. 28/2016 as amended). Investor PRCs existed before 2012 (the 2009 Auld inquiry recorded complaints of grants for bribes); a moratorium and 2012 reform left only a 10-year investor residence permit, and an investor PRC route was reintroduced in 2013. Routes: home of US$1m (US$300,000 on Grand Turk and family islands), business of US$1.5m (US$750,000) employing at least 60% non-work-permit holders, US$1m contribution to a designated public project, or US$1m in a home or business. US$25,000 fee. Investment must be kept 5 years (since June 2018). The Governor must set a quota; none was found published. PRC does not give British Overseas Territories citizenship. No official counts found.

programs.name: Turks and Caicos Islands Residence Permit for investors (condition B, Immigration Regulations reg 24)
programs.notes: Temporary residence permit (up to 10 years, renewable, per the 2012 announcement) for investors of US$500,000 in a business or home on Providenciales or West Caicos, or US$250,000 on Grand Turk, Salt Cay, South Caicos, Middle Caicos or North Caicos; no work beyond overseeing the investment. Holding a residence permit for 10+ years is itself a route to a PRC. Fee US$1,500.

programs.name: Anguilla Residence by Investment (Anguilla Economic Residence Act 2019)
programs.notes: Permanent residence through approved real estate (US$750,000 for a family of four, 5-year hold) or a contribution to the Capital Development Fund (US$150,000 single applicant; not usable until the fund was set up, after December 2022). Run by the Select Anguilla Agency through authorised agents. A retroactive route covered owners of property bought before 31 May 2019 (US$500,000-750,000 depending on purchase date). The same Act offers tax residence (US$75,000 a year). An amending Act and Regulations were passed in 2024 (not retrieved). Permanent residence does not give Belonger status; naturalisation needs years of residence. No counts found.

programs.name: Barbados Special Entry and Reside Permit (SERP)
programs.notes: Long-term or indefinite residence permit granted by varying permission to stay under s.13(3) of the Immigration Act, Cap. 190. According to practitioner sources (not confirmed officially): Category 1 for investors of US$2m with net worth over US$5m (with work permit eligibility); Category 2 for owners of US$300,000 of real estate (5-year renewable, indefinite from age 60). Launch date and legal instrument not found. Listed by the OECD in 2018 as potentially high-risk for CRS avoidance. No counts found.

programs.name: Dominican Republic residence by investment (residencia por inversión)
programs.notes: Investor residence processed by the Dirección General de Migración on the basis of an investment certified by ProDominicana; integrated into the single investment window in 2024. Legal basis believed to be the General Migration Law 285-04 and its Regulation (Decree 631-11), with Law 171-07 for pensioners and rentiers, but the provisions were not read. Minimum amount not confirmed: the Migration director cited US$250,000 in 2021; advisers commonly cite US$200,000. No counts found.
